name: Protectores Domestici Pedites

abilities.name: Spear Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

abilities.name: Testudo
abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a defensive formation.

abilities.name: Shield Screen
abilities.text: The unit raises their shields in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Square
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close square formation. Note that it cannot move whilst this ability is active.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Formation Attack
attributes.text: The unit will try to stay in formation when in melee.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Protector Domesticus translates as «household guard». An honorary title in the Roman army from the 3rd century onwards, and from the 4th century as bodyguards of the first persons of the Empire. The title of protector dates back to the middle of the 3rd century, then it was used only as a title of honor or simply a title of domestic servant; this designation meant only that these men were attached to the imperial family (domus). Beginning under Diocletian, the term was used to refer to a small unit of the imperial court. In 346 the domestici appeared as a corps and formed two scholae, one of infantry and the other of cavalry, each consisting of 500 men and under the command of the comes domesticorum. Unlike the imperial guard (scholae palatinae), the protectores domestici were not intended to fight alongside the Emperor. In fact, they performed a variety of tasks: they accompanied the Emperor or senior officers, acted as communication and intelligence officers, and could also be sent to arrest or assassinate high-ranking officials. Ammianus Marcellinus, who was himself a protector domesticus, tells how his group was sent by Constantius II to Gaul to eliminate the usurper Silvanus in 355 AD.
history: 'Auxilia palatina' were elite auxiliary troops that first emerged from the military reforms and expansion of Constantine the Great in AD325. Drafted from the local populace, auxiliaries often took the name of the tribe from which they were predominantly comprised, such as the Mattiaci and the Ampsivarii. The Notitia Dignitatum gives a fairly comprehensive list of units classified as auxilia palatina but does not give any direct reference to the strength of those troops. However, there is some confusion between auxilia and limitanei, who were specifically frontier troops. It can be assumed, therefore, that auxilia palatina were stationed in force behind the Empire's frontiers, in such places as Gaul, Iberia and Britannia.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
